# Common Log Format Parsing

Apache's **Common Log Format** (CLF) and its **Combined** extension look space-separated and are not:

```
host ident authuser [timestamp] "request" status bytes "referer" "user-agent"
```

Three of the nine fields are quoted — `request`, `referer`, `user-agent` — and they are quoted
*because they contain spaces*. The bracketed timestamp contains a space too. So `line.split()` does
not merely fail on those fields; it shifts every field after the first quoted one, silently.

> "Parsing is one regular expression, not `line.split()`. The request, referer and user-agent fields
> are quoted precisely because they contain spaces, so positional indexing shifts every field after
> the first quoted one — silently, producing plausible wrong answers rather than an error."
> — Python-Programming-Laboratories/README.md, 2026-07-25

That is the whole argument: the failure produces **plausible wrong answers**, not an exception. A
status-code histogram built on shifted fields still looks like a status-code histogram. The decision
is recorded on [[regex-over-split-for-log-parsing]].

## The quoted-field subtlety

The obvious pattern for a quoted field, `"[^"]*"`, is wrong as soon as a value contains a
backslash-escaped quote. The correct form is:

```
(?:[^"\\]|\\.)*
```

— any character that is neither a quote nor a backslash, **or** a backslash followed by anything.
This is not a hypothetical hardening:

> "Not hypothetical -- the sample log in data/ contains an injection attempt whose referer embeds \"
> sequences, and a naive [^\"]* would terminate the field at the first inner quote and reject the
> whole line."
> — Python-Programming-Laboratories/src/weblog/entry.py, 2026-07-25

The attack traffic in a real log is precisely the traffic most likely to break a naive parser — so a
parser that drops malformed lines drops the lines you most wanted to see.

## Around the regex

- One `re.VERBOSE` pattern covering both CLF and Combined, so the parser is readable and commentable
  rather than a wall of escapes.
- A frozen, slotted `LogEntry` dataclass whose `__str__` **round-trips back to CLF** — parse and
  re-emit is an identity, which is a testable property rather than an assertion. See
  [[pythons-data-model]].
- Lazy `iter_entries` generator: a log is streamed, never loaded.
- A `ParseReport` counting skipped lines and retaining the first five, so failures are surfaced with
  examples instead of swallowed. `errors="replace"` on decode means a bad byte costs one skipped line,
  not the run.
